 Order
21.02.2023 Order No.
05. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.

This is an application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with T.R.
Case No.41 of 2022 arising out of Kalimela P.S. Case No.197 of 2022 pending in the file of learned Addl. Sessions Judge-Cum-Special Judge, Malkangiri, for commission of offences punishable under Sections 363/ 366-A/ 376(2)(n)/ 342/ 306/ 417/ 506/ 109/ 34 of IPC read with Section 6/17 of POCSO Act, on the main allegation of kidnapping and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the victim as well as abetting the commission of suicide of the victim.
3.

In the course of hearing of the bail application, Mr. A.K. Sahoo, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that even if all the materials on record are taken into consideration, no offence is stated to be made out against the present petitioner and the petitioner has been detained in custody since 31.07.2022 and in the meanwhile, charge-sheet has already been submitted in this case, but the present petitioner having falsely implicated in this case, may kindly be granted bail.
4. On the contrary, Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned AGA, however, by placing the statement of the father of the victim, prays to reject the bail application of the petitioner.

sentences.text: 1 5. Ms. R. Singh, learned counsel for the informant, however, strongly, opposes the bail application of the petitioner and she interalia submits that due to blackmailing of the petitioner, the deceased committed suicide and, thereby, the present petitioner may not be granted bail.

6. After considering the rival submissions made and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of allegations raised against the petitioner and keeping in view the manner and circumstance of death of a minor girl and regard being had to the peculiarity of the nature of allegation raised against the present petitioner and on going through the materials placed on record including the cause of death of the deceased, this Court does not find any justification grant bail to the petitioner,
at this stage, when the trial is yet to commence.
7. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands rejected.
8. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
9. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy) Judge Subhasmita Subhankar Ray @ Shubamkar vs State Of Orissa ...
